headline: PLS.AX surges 4% to lead the ASX portfolio today, while US markets and indices await tonight's open.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara jumped 4.1% today to $5.36 — a strong single-session bounce for a stock that's been under pressure. No specific news catalyst available, but lithium sentiment has been improving as markets watch for any signs of a demand pickup from Chinese battery makers. Still well below your cost base, but today's move is encouraging.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Nudged up 0.25% today to $93.93. Emerging markets have been getting a mild lift from a slightly softer US dollar. No dramatic news — just steady drift.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Ticked up 0.23% today to $77.19, just edging into positive territory overall (+$1.51). The broad diversified ETF followed the general tone of a quiet but slightly positive ASX session.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Gained a modest 0.18% today to $16.31. Still sitting well below your average cost (down ~13.6% overall), but at least the AI theme has stabilised for now. No specific news catalyst today.

movers.note: Rose 0.16% today to $528.61 — this ETF tracks the US sharemarket and moves with Wall Street sentiment. Up 2.5% overall on your position. US markets haven't opened yet tonight, so watch for any after-hours moves.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Strong bounce, but long-term picture unchanged
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals jumped 4.1% today to $5.36 — a welcome move, but you're still down about 20% on your position. There's no major news catalyst behind today's pop, so don't read too much into it as a trend reversal. The long-term story depends on a lithium demand recovery, which is still playing out. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — Small bounce, still deep in the red
watch_today.detail: The AI ETF crept up 0.18% today but is still down 13.6% overall. If you believe AI is a decade-long theme (and the evidence is strong), this is still a hold — but know that this ETF is volatile and linked to US tech sentiment, which can swing hard overnight.

watch_today.detail: GOOG (last $337.71 USD), MSFT (last $505.06 USD), and TTWO (last $233.00 USD) haven't traded yet tonight. No major news flagged for any of these today. Check prices tomorrow morning.

watch_today.title: AUD/USD dipped to 71.64 US cents
watch_today.detail: The Aussie dollar slipped 0.43% to 71.64 US cents. A weaker AUD is actually a tailwind for your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) and VTS.AX — when the AUD falls, the AUD value of your US investments rises. Worth keeping an eye on if the trend continues.

watch_today.title: VTS.AX and VDHG.AX — Quiet green day, all good
watch_today.detail: Both Vanguard ETFs ticked up modestly today (VTS +0.16%, VDHG +0.23%). Nothing to act on — just steady long-term compounding doing its thing. Hold and let them run.

sport.summary: Big Round 26 NRL action this weekend — the Storm thrashed the Broncos in Brisbane, the Dolphins upset the Roosters, and the Rabbitohs ran riot against the Gold Coast Titans. Panthers and Cowboys also won comfortably.

stories.title: Storm smash Broncos 46-20 at Suncorp Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm put on a clinic in Brisbane on Thursday night, running out 46-20 winners. A massive statement win for the Storm in enemy territory at Suncorp — tough night for Broncos fans in the crowd.

stories.title: Dolphins upset Roosters 26-12 at Allianz Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins continued their strong form, beating the Sydney Roosters 26-12 on Saturday afternoon. A 14-point win away from home is a real confidence boost for the Dolphins as finals race heats up.

stories.title: Rabbitohs run riot over Titans 42-22 at Cbus Super Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: Tough afternoon for local Gold Coast fans — the Titans were beaten soundly at home by South Sydney, 42-22. The Rabbitohs were dominant and the scoreline flatters the Titans.

stories.title: Panthers beat Bulldogs 24-10, Cowboys down Tigers 24-10
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith showed finals form with a comfortable 24-10 win over Canterbury on Friday night at CommBank Stadium. Up in Townsville, the Cowboys were equally dominant over the Wests Tigers by the same 24-10 scoreline on Saturday night. Both clubs look well-placed heading into finals.

stories.title: Sea Eagles thump Dragons 44-10 at 4 Pines Park
stories.why_it_matters: Manly put on a 44-10 demolition of St George Illawarra on Friday evening — a massive winning margin that boosts their for-and-against as the finals race tightens. Dragons' season continues to spiral.
